legend: After a long day, Alice and Bob decided to play a little game. The game board consists of n%%ZSMJ0%% cells in a straight line, numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%%, where each cell contains a number ai%%ZSMJ3%% between 1%%ZSMJ4%% and n%%ZSMJ5%%. Furthermore, no two cells contain the same number.

A token is placed in one of the cells. They take alternating turns of moving the token around the board, with Alice moving first. The current player can move from cell i%%ZSMJ6%% to cell j%%ZSMJ7%% only if the following two conditions are satisfied:
the number in the new cell j%%ZSMJ8%% must be strictly larger than the number in the old cell i%%ZSMJ9%% (i.e. aj>ai%%ZSMJ10%%), and
the distance that the token travels during this turn must be a multiple of the number in the old cell (i.e. |i−j|modai=0%%ZSMJ11%%).

Whoever is unable to make a move, loses. For each possible starting position, determine who wins if they both play optimally. It can be shown that the game is always finite, i.e. there always is a winning strategy for one of the players.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of numbers.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ14%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤ai≤n%%ZSMJ16%%). Furthermore, there are no pair of indices i≠j%%ZSMJ17%% such that ai=aj%%ZSMJ18%%.
output: Print s%%ZSMJ19%% — a string of n%%ZSMJ20%% characters, where the i%%ZSMJ21%%-th character represents the outcome of the game if the token is initially placed in the cell i%%ZSMJ22%%. If Alice wins, then si%%ZSMJ23%% has to be equal to "A"; otherwise, si%%ZSMJ24%% has to be equal to "B".
note: In the first sample, if Bob puts the token on the number (not position):
1%%ZSMJ25%%: Alice can move to any number. She can win by picking 7%%ZSMJ26%%, from which Bob has no move.

2%%ZSMJ27%%: Alice can move to 3%%ZSMJ28%% and 5%%ZSMJ29%%. Upon moving to 5%%ZSMJ30%%, Bob can win by moving to 8%%ZSMJ31%%. If she chooses 3%%ZSMJ32%% instead, she wins, as Bob has only a move to 4%%ZSMJ33%%, from which Alice can move to 8%%ZSMJ34%%.
3%%ZSMJ35%%: Alice can only move to 4%%ZSMJ36%%, after which Bob wins by moving to 8%%ZSMJ37%%.
4%%ZSMJ38%%, 5%%ZSMJ39%%, or 6%%ZSMJ40%%: Alice wins by moving to 8%%ZSMJ41%%.
7%%ZSMJ42%%, 8%%ZSMJ43%%: Alice has no move, and hence she loses immediately.
